result.reason: The baraita introduces the dual penalty of lashes and one hundred sela, which is precisely what the 'Lashes & Payment' section's prose describes as its topic, before Rabbi Yehuda's qualification is discussed separately in the next section.

All five items discuss the mapping of the baraita's dispute onto Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov vs. Rabbanan regarding the sex requirement, the two readings of the baraita (items 1-2), and the challenge/resolution regarding Rabbi Yehuda's position on lashes and money (items 3-5), which is precisely what the 'Sex Requirement' prose describes.

The prose under 'Lashes Explained' explicitly discusses all six items: the baraita on v'anshu/veyisru, Rabbi Abbahu's chain derivation, and the dispute between Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Natan over the prohibitory lav for motzi shem ra, including why each sage doesn't use the other's verse.

All six items deal with the defamer case where witnesses testify on their own accord, Rabbi Yehuda's requirement of hiring witnesses, the gezeira shava of 'sima sima,' and Rabbi Yirmeyah's unresolved dilemmas — all of which are explicitly discussed in the 'Witness Liability' prose.

Both items — Rav Ashi's dilemmas about defaming regarding a first marriage or a brother's marriage, and the resolution from Rabbi Yona's baraita excluding the yavam — are precisely what the 'Edge Cases' prose discusses in detail.

All 8 items comprise the baraita describing the defamation procedure and the systematic pesuk-by-pesuk analysis of the dispute between the Rabbis and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, which is precisely what the 'Pesuk Analysis' prose describes in detail.

All three items form a continuous Talmudic discussion about the kedarkah/shelo kedarkah distinction in motzi shem ra, which is exactly what the 'Kedarkah' section's prose describes in detail, including the same Rabbi Yochanan ruling, the same challenge about the Rabbanan vs. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, and Rav Kahana's correction.

The Mishnah passage covers the full range of paternal rights including betrothal modes, found items, earnings, vow nullification, and get reception — the prose under 'Paternal Rights' (index 1) introduces this entire Mishnah, while index 2 only discusses the secondary rights beyond betrothal, making index 1 the correct home for the complete Mishnah text.

The passage covers both the husband's additional rights (peiros) and his obligations (sustenance, redemption, burial) plus Rabbi Yehuda's minimum burial requirement, which maps precisely to the 'Obligations' section prose rather than the 'Husband's Rights' section which focuses only on the rights/peiros aspect.
The passage directly addresses deriving the father's entitlement to betrothal money from the verse about the Hebrew maidservant, which is precisely what the 'Money Source' section's prose discusses.

The passage directly addresses the question of whether the betrothal money goes to the daughter herself and refutes it using the verse 'I gave my daughter to this man,' which is precisely what the 'Father as Master' section's prose describes.

The passage raises the ketanah/naarah distinction and then answers it with the verse — the entire unit (question + answer) belongs under 'Ketanah vs Naarah', which describes exactly this dialectic, while the current heading 'Shevach Ne'urim' describes only the aftermath/continuation of that answer.
